mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 1.5% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during the identified tightening phase.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment growth) of at least 50,000 jobs coincides with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as labor market strength supports corporate optimism and investment.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with PAYEMS monthly change (Pearson r < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) exceeds 800K units in two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive, reflecting stronger consumer demand and corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite the demand signal (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of 2% or more predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as weak manufacturing signals contractionary conditions.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during INDPRO declines of ≥2%.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in both CPIAUCSL (CPI) and FEDFUNDS by 0.5% each create a reinforcing negative signal that drives a negative S&P 20-day forward return due to expectations of slower inflation and tighter policy.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < prev AND FEDFUNDS < prev for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite the dual decline (IC > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE (unemployment) below 4% triggers a positive S&P 20-day forward return as low labor market friction supports market optimism.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the low-unemployment regime.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (GDP) grows at an annualized rate above 4% over the prior quarter, the S&P 60-day forward return is positive, reflecting strong aggregate demand and investor confidence.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no correlation with quarterly GDP growth (Spearman ρ < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in RSAFS (retail sales of financial assets) of 10% or more indicates investor pessimism, leading to a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly < prev * 0.9 for two months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the RSAFS decline period.
